subject: Onboarding stress-proof: FastLedger benchmarking & handoff
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@fastledger.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@fastledger.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria for phase 1

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — FastLedger is excited to move into the onboarding benchmark run for our invoice summarization pipeline. We want to align on acceptance criteria and logistics so we can complete our procurement signoff. High level asks: 

- Confirm latency (p95) and throughput targets you expect for our N=1k concurrent users testing pattern.
- Share the load script you'll use and any specific headers/keys we should include (we'll run from our staging VPC).
- Tell us which artifacts you want back (wire logs, token breakdown, telemetry).

Proposed target (from our side): sustained 1800 RPS for 10 minutes with p95 <= 220ms for the text-generation endpoint; tail latency under 500ms. If Redwood has standard quantization/batching profiles you recommend for Retail-XL2-v1, please advise.

Can you send a runbook and preferred windows (we can run tests Thursday morning PST or Friday afternoon PST)?

Thanks,
Asha
--
Asha Menon
Director, Engineering Operations
FastLedger
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Menon <asha@fastledger.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria for phase 1

Hi Asha — great to be moving forward. Quick responses inline, and attaching the runbook and a canonical JMeter script we typically ask customers to use. Attachments: redwood-evidence-20290515.zip (runbook + telemetry schema), fastledger-loadscript-20290514.jmx (example), test-results-template.csv (expected CSV layout).

Targets we recommend for your workload (based on your demo traces and our perf model):
- Sustained throughput target: 1600–1800 RPS (we can push to 2k in bursts).
- Latency SLO (p95): <= 200ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens); <= 300ms for longer prompts (~512 tokens).
- Tail: 99th <= 650ms (we'll aim to tune to 500ms once caching is validated).

Notes on profile and gating:
- Use Retail-XL2-v1-quant (8-bit) for the initial run; we'll route to full-precision only if accuracy/regression needs it.
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated prefixes — we'll provide a test corpus with repeated invoice headers to validate effectiveness.
- Batching: start with batch size 8 and concurrency stepped every 2 minutes to track latency inflection.

Run windows: Thursday 05/16 08:00–12:00 PST works for our infra team; we can also do Friday 05/17 13:00–16:00 PST if you prefer. 

Deliverables we'll produce after the run:
1) test-results-summary-20290515.csv (latency percentiles, RPS timeline)
2) redwood-evidence-20290515.zip (traces, token-level cost breakdown)
3) short readout + suggested tuning checklist for production rollout.

Action items for FastLedger before Thursday:
- Confirm which window you prefer.
- Provide access IP ranges from your staging VPC and the set of prompt templates for prefix caching.

I'll loop in Monica and Karthik for telemetry and kernel tuning follow-up.

Best,
Mina
--
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Menon <asha@fastledger.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@fastledger.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 07:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria for phase 1

Thanks Mina — Thursday morning works. We're provisioned to run 08:30 PST. Two quick items before kickoff: 

1) Staging IPs: 34.58.12.0/24 and 35.12.220.5 (we'll open ephemeral ports 443 and 8443).
2) Prompt bundles: attached (invoice-prompts-v1.jsonl). We'll also include a subset intended to exercise repeated prefixes so your caching can warm.

We'll run the JMeter script largely untouched but will set header X-Client-ID: fastledger-staging and include the test API key you provided in the runbook. Expect the initial ramp from 200 -> 1600 RPS over 12 minutes, hold 10 minutes, then ramp down. We'll upload the raw JMeter logs and a CSV conforming to your template to the Drive link at the end of the run.

See you at 08:30 PT.

--
Asha
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Menon <asha@fastledger.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking kickoff + acceptance criteria for phase 1

Asha — quick readout from our side. We captured the run artifacts and preliminary numbers; full packet with traces attached (redwood-evidence-20290515.zip). Summary highlights: 

- Peak sustained RPS held: 1,750 RPS (12-minute hold).
- Average p95 observed for test set: 188ms (short prompts), 274ms (long prompts).
- 99th percentile: 498ms (within our optimistic tail target).
- Observed KV cache hit-rate on repeated prefixes: ~46% after 4 minutes of warm-up; we expect >60% after a longer warm-up or if FastLedger precaches the common invoice headers.
- Token-level cost delta vs full-precision: ~26% reduction using Retail-XL2-v1-quant with identical accuracy on your eval set.

Attached artifacts: test-results-summary-20290515.csv (CSV with percentile breakdown + RPS timeline), raw traces and token breakdown in the zip, and the annotated runbook page that lists a few follow-ups: 
- Short-term: increase prefix warm-up window and precache top 10 invoice prefixes; bump batch size to 12 for longer prompts if tail remains stable.
- Mid-term: consider a canary route using full-precision for 5% of traffic to validate no edge regressions under production traffic.

Next steps/action owners: 
- FastLedger: try precache + re-run one 10-minute hold to confirm hit-rate improvement (Asha).
- Redwood infra: prepare a canary routing config and a short rollback plan (Monica).
- CS: finalize acceptance note and include the artifacts for procurement (Mina).

If procurement needs a formal acceptance memo (signed), we'll draft one with the final CSV attached. Otherwise, let us know if the artifacts here suffice for your signoff.

Thanks team — nice run.

Best,
Mina
--
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
